results.title: Ghana’s 2027 Budget: From macroeconomic stability to prioritising public investment
results.content: The 2026 economic outturn supports the government’s claim that stabilisation has advanced. Real GDP grew 6.2% in the first half of 2026; headline inflation was 5.5% in October. During January–October, the commitment-basis primary surplus reached 1.4% of GDP, and the cash deficit was 2.3% of GDP against a programmed 4.5%. Public debt stood at 47.5% of GDP at end-October. Average commercial-bank lending rates had fallen to about 15.9%, while private-sector credit was expanding at 34% year on year in September. These developments suggest that Ghana’s macroeconomic conditions are generally moving in a favorable direction, providing a stronger foundation for sustained economic stability and growth.

results.title: Achievements of ‘New Economy’ must be measured by sustained improvements in economic growth, employment and productivity – Dr. Nsafoah
results.content: In his commentary on the budget titled “Ghana's 2027 Budget: From Macroeconomic Stability to Prioritising Public Investment”, Dr. Nsafoah said the 2027 Budget identifies a markedly larger public investment envelope, communicates a mainly domestic financing strategy and offers a measured formal reserve-adequacy benchmark. “These are reasons for a constructive assessment, not a guarantee of success”.

results.title: Methane cuts offer cheap, fast route to tackling global warming – UN climate chief
results.content: UN Climate Change Executive Secretary Simon Stiell has urged governments to accelerate efforts to reduce methane and other super pollutants, describing them as one of the fastest, cheapest and most effective ways to slow global heating in the near term. He says tackling these emissions could also generate significant economic gains, improve public health and strengthen agricultural production.

results.title: NACOC arrests man who allegedly swallowed 58 cocaine pellets before India trip
results.content: The Narcotics Control Commission (NACOC) has arrested a 58-year-old man at the Accra International Airport after he was reportedly found to have swallowed 58 pellets suspected to contain cocaine. The suspect was preparing to travel to India when he was identified during the Commission’s routine passenger pre-screening operations. According to NACOC, subsequent examination revealed that he had ingested the pellets in an apparent attempt to conceal the suspected narcotic substance and transport it across international borders.
